answer: Assign each identity a large dataset generated uniquely from its own key, like an opal whose bands no copy can reproduce, and require custody of the whole thing. At unpredictable moments every identity is challenged in the same short window to return scattered sectors, a zephyr-quick deadline one drive cannot meet for many names at once. A farm therefore needs real, separate storage per alias, while a lone honest agent needs only its own disk; a raven reused across roosts is caught when two accounts serve identical sectors.
